churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.

The 2024 UMC General Conference removed all language restricting LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage. With a female senior pastor, multiple associate pastors, and UMC denominational accountability to a now-affirming hierarchy, this church does not align with Moop's theological convictions. The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.

churches.assessment: Trinity Episcopal has the same fundamental problem as St. George's Episcopal: it belongs to The Episcopal Church (TEC), which has made formal, binding institutional commitments to LGBTQ+ affirmation that place it outside biblical alignment. The rector lists she/her pronouns on the church website, men serve with he/him pronouns listed — pronoun-aware staff culture is a visible marker of TEC's progressive institutional identity. Founded in 1877, Trinity has a rich liturgical history and likely has sincere Christians in the congregation, but the denominational framework and leadership culture are incompatible with Moop's convictions. The 'inclusive community of seekers' branding further flags a therapeutic/inclusive ecclesiology rather than a word-and-sacrament Great Commission model. Not recommended.

The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

churches.assessment: Selah is a young, Spirit-filled church led by genuinely gospel-loving people. Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. But structural concerns are real: no elder accountability, women functioning in pastoral roles, and a spiritual formation emphasis that can trend contemplative rather than expository. If you're a man who needs clear authority structures and complementarian conviction, visit with your eyes open. If you're a new believer or seeking family, you'll find genuine love here. Just ask the hard questions early.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.

churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

churches.assessment: Common Ground Church has a compelling origin story: 21 years as a mobile congregation finally receiving a permanent home — the historic First Christian Church building on Washington Ave, gifted free of charge by a 100-year-old congregation choosing to bless its successor. churches.assessment: St. Jude's Anglican Church is an REC/ACNA congregation in Richmond — and the Reformed Episcopal Church is one of the most doctrinally rigorous Anglican bodies in existence. Founded in 1873 as a protest against Catholic ritualism in the Anglican tradition, the REC holds to Protestant soteriology (justification by faith alone), Reformation Anglican standards (39 Articles, Book of Common Prayer), male-only clergy, and traditional biblical ethics. Very Rev. W. Scott Thompson leads a congregation described as 'a traditional congregation focused on Jesus Christ, His Gospel, and worship through Word and Sacrament.' This is exactly the kind of clarity men committed to Reformed orthodoxy need: no ambiguity on gender, no denominational drift, no social justice crowding out the Gospel. The REC/ACNA dual affiliation means accountability in both the richest Reformed Anglican tradition and the broader ACNA network. One of the strongest options for any man who loves liturgy, Reformed soteriology, and biblical authority.

churches.assessment: The Falls Church Anglican has one of the most remarkable stories in American Christianity. As one of America's oldest churches (1734), it separated from The Episcopal Church over homosexuality and women's ordination, fought a legal battle that cost them their historic building, and re-planted as a faithful Anglican congregation. They now worship at an office building — having chosen doctrinal integrity over real estate. Rector Sam Ferguson leads a congregation with deep roots in biblical Anglicanism, liturgical worship rooted in Scripture, and a legacy of sending. ACNA accountability, male-only priesthood, complementarian household vision. For a man who values covenantal worship, historic liturgy, and a congregation that has paid a price for orthodoxy — this is worth serious consideration.

Mahaney as a charismatic fellowship, it evolved into one of America's most theologically sophisticated Reformed evangelical churches — hosting conferences, producing discipleship resources, and nurturing a generation of serious Bible-saturated Christians. But CLC also became ground zero for significant controversies: the Sovereign Grace Churches abuse lawsuit (2012), C.J. Mahaney's leadership scandals, and most publicly — Joshua Harris (pastor 2004-2015) publicly deconstructing his faith in 2019 and renouncing Christianity. Current pastor Mark Mitchell leads a congregation that has weathered enormous institutional trauma. The theological framework (Reformed, complementarian, Gospel-centered) remains intact on paper. The questions are about institutional health, pastoral culture, and whether the congregation has genuinely processed and healed from years of controversy. Worth visiting with eyes wide open.

churches.assessment: Pohick Church is one of the oldest and most historically significant churches in Northern Virginia — originally built in 1774 and known as the parish of George Washington, George Mason, and other Virginia Founders. It is a landmark of American religious history. However, it remains affiliated with the Episcopal Church (TEC), which has undergone systematic theological abandonment since the 1970s — ordaining women as priests and bishops, affirming same-sex marriage, and ordaining LGBTQ+ clergy. The historic beauty of this church and its colonial American legacy are genuinely compelling, but the TEC institutional framework is doctrinally unreliable. Men seeking sound biblical preaching and complementarian theology should consider ACNA alternatives in Northern Virginia (such as The Falls Church Anglican or Truro Anglican), which left TEC precisely over these issues. Visit Pohick as a history lesson; find a sound church for your soul.

The church is led by a well-educated pastor, Victor (Vic) Carpenter, who holds a Ph.D. from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Their leadership structure includes a plurality of male elders, and they have dedicated ministries for men, women, and children. For anyone seeking a complementarian, SBC-affiliated church with a high view of Scripture and a commitment to discipleship and church planting, Redeemer Bible Church is an excellent option in the Spotsylvania area. MOOP-context note (Adam Johns, 2026): Adam attended both Redeemer Bible Spotsy and Stafford and characterizes the network as "splants" from his home church Spotswood Baptist — the new chain catered to Spotswood members who were "more Calvinist leaning" than Spotswood's SBC mainstream. Worth understanding as inheritor of Spotswood's baseline orthodoxy + Reformed-Baptist refinement.

churches.assessment: All Saints Church in New Holland, PA (Lancaster County) was established in 1999 as a church plant of Christ Church (Moscow, ID) and is a member of the CREC. Dr. Gregg Strawbridge served faithfully as pastor for twenty years (2002–2022) and is the founder of the Strawbridge Ministerial Forum hosted by the church. Following his passing in 2022, Rev. Kasey Horvath (lead) and Rev. Brandon Gilanyi (associate) were installed in 2023, and the congregation relocated to a historic building in New Holland in 2024. Theologically this is a classic Moscow-network CREC congregation: Reformed, covenant-renewal liturgical worship, paedocommunion, classical Christian education ethos, patriarchal household vision, and postmillennial cultural engagement. The one area calling for direct inquiry is soteriology — CREC churches have historically been associated with Federal Vision theology, which modifies traditional Reformed articulations of justification. Ask the elders directly about their position on FV and justification. For a Reformed man in Lancaster County seeking a serious, liturgical, Moscow-aligned CREC home, this is the obvious first visit.

In Beaufort SC, there is no church currently operating as 'First Baptist Church Beaufort.' The historic SBC-affiliated Baptist church in Beaufort SC is 'The Baptist Church of Beaufort' (bcob.org, 601 Charles Street, Beaufort SC) — founded 1804, oldest surviving congregation in town, SC Baptist Convention affiliated. Other Beaufort SC Baptist churches include First African Baptist Church (fabbeaufort.org, Pastor Alexander McBride) and Victory Baptist Church (independent fundamental, 378 Parris Island Gateway).
churches.review_question: The record identity 'First Baptist Beaufort SC' may not correspond to any real church. churches.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

The church's mission — 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household' — reflects a patriarchal, family-centered, Great Commission focus. Elder Alex Kocman's role with ABWE, his published work at American Reformer and Founders Ministries, and his hands-on men's discipleship leadership give the church unusually strong DNA on biblical manhood, male headship, and international missions. churches.assessment: Salt Church in Hartfield, VA is a scrappy church plant on the Chesapeake Bay led by John Michael Clark — a 13-year ordained minister who also runs The Family Captain, a coaching ministry for Christian men on family leadership and marriage. churches.assessment: The Woodlands Methodist Church is the single largest church in the Global Methodist Church — 14,000 members who voted 96% to depart the UMC and join the GMC in 2023. That kind of institutional courage (leaving a denomination with all the attendant property and legal costs) signals a congregation serious about orthodox Wesleyan teaching. Rev. Mark Sorensen took over as Senior Pastor from the long-tenured Rev. Dr. Ed Robb in 2021, holds an M.Div from Asbury Theological Seminary, and has served the church since 2013. The church operates two campuses in the Houston suburbs, runs a preschool and a private elementary school, and offers 10 live and online worship services weekly. As with all GMC churches, the local stance on women as elders should be verified (the Texas conference varies), but the overall profile is solidly orthodox, Trinitarian, traditional-marriage Wesleyan.

churches.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Columbia, South Carolina (ARP) is one of the most historically significant orthodox Reformed congregations in the United States. The 1854 church building is on the National Register of Historic Places (added January 1971). The pulpit lineage includes James Henley Thornwell, Benjamin Morgan Palmer, John Girardeau, and more recently Sinclair Ferguson and Derek Thomas — a roll call of Reformed theological heavyweights. The congregation principled-seceded from the mainline Presbyterian Church in the United States in 1983 and joined the ARP to preserve its confessional identity. Dr. Neil C. Stewart currently serves as Senior Minister and Head of Staff. Three Sunday services (8:30 AM, 11:15 AM, and 6:00 PM). ARP confessional framework with male-only ordination aligns with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. One of the strongest possible green-rated Reformed Presbyterian options in the Southeast, though note that the church's website currently displays 'Presbyterian Church (USA)' in some metadata — this appears to be outdated website text; per the ARP official directory and Wikipedia, the church has been ARP since 1983.

churches.assessment: The Bible Presbyterian Church on Grand Island, New York is part of the Bible Presbyterian Church's Great Lakes Presbytery. Senior Pastor Dr. Kevin M. Backus holds a Ph.D. — unusually strong academic credentials for a small-denomination pastor. The BPC was formed in 1937 by Carl McIntire, J. Oliver Buswell, and Allan MacRae as a conservative fundamentalist-leaning breakaway Presbyterian denomination holding the Westminster Standards with a pronounced emphasis on biblical inerrancy and separation from liberalism. The denomination is very small (only 28 churches across the US and one in Canada) — MOOP readers considering BPC congregations should understand they will likely find a small, tight-knit, strongly-convictional Reformed fellowship rather than a large-church experience. Green-rated orthodox Reformed option for the Buffalo, NY metro.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Church of Hammond is the historic Hyles-Anderson legacy IFB congregation in Hammond, IN. The church is tied to Hyles-Anderson College and was led by Jack Hyles from 1959 until his death in 2001, then by his son-in-law Jack Schaap from 2001 until Schaap's 2012 conviction for sexual misconduct with a 16-year-old church member (he served prison time and was released 2021). Multiple women have publicly described abuse and cover-up patterns spanning decades of the Hyles era. Current senior pastor John Wilkerson (since 2013) inherited the institution at its lowest reputational point and has publicly acknowledged the failures while leading reform. The congregation is included for completeness as one of the most consequential IFB institutions in the country, but is rated YELLOW with significant caution: the documented abuse history, Hyles-era pastor-as-king theology, and KJV-Only doctrinal emphasis all warrant discernment. Adam should not visit casually; survivors of Hyles/Schaap-era abuse remain a live pastoral concern within IFB circles.

churches.assessment: Wilshire Baptist Church is a former-SBC, former-BGCT congregation in Dallas that was formally removed from BGCT cooperation in February 2017 after voting in November 2016 to affirm LGBTQ members in full church life including same-sex marriage and deacon service. The church currently lists Heather Mustain as Associate Pastor and two female Pastoral Residents (Amanda Hines, Jordann McMahan), placing it in direct conflict with BF&M 2000 Article VI on the office of pastor. Documented as a leading drift reference case for Texas SBC/BGCT.
churches.gender_detail: Heather Mustain — Associate Pastor (since 2013, current 2026 staff page wilshirebc.org/about/our-staff/); Amanda Hines and Jordann McMahan — Pastoral Residents (began Aug 2025); Katie Murray — Minister of Pastoral Care and to Senior Adults. All female pastoral titles confirmed on current Wilshire staff page.
churches.denomination_detail: Founded 1952 in BGCT; formally disfellowshipped by BGCT Executive Board February 2017 by 63-6 vote following Wilshire's November 2016 LGBTQ-affirming vote. Now affiliated with Cooperative Baptist Fellowship (Partner) and Association of Welcoming & Affirming Baptists.
churches.enrichment_notes: Verified 2026-05-01: Wilshire staff page lists Heather Mustain as Associate Pastor + 3 additional female pastoral-titled staff. BGCT disfellowship documented via Baptist News Global and CBS News. Address from church website. Pattern reference precedent per scope.

The congregation is fully LGBTQIA+ welcoming and affirming, was previously declared out of fellowship with the Dallas Baptist Association over ordaining a practicing-homosexual deacon, and aligns with CBF and the Alliance of Baptists. churches.assessment: Greater Tabernacle Missionary Baptist (Lawrenceburg TN) called Rev. Shonda Reynolds Christian as senior pastor in June 2015 and was disfellowshipped by the Lawrence County Association of Baptists by a 73-4 vote on October 12, 2015 — the association explicitly citing the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 Article VI ('the office of pastor is limited to men as qualified by Scripture'). Pastor Christian, who continues to lead the church a decade later, publicly characterized the disfellowship as 'unchristian' and challenged the binding force of the 2000 BF&M revision. This case set the early modern precedent for SBC state-association action against churches with female senior pastors and remains the longest-running Mid-South case.

churches.assessment: The View Church (Menifee, CA) is a fast-growing African-American SBC congregation under lead pastor Gregory Perkins, who serves as president of the National African American Fellowship of the SBC. churches.assessment: Historic First Baptist Church of Beech Island is an 1832-founded SBC-affiliated Baptist congregation in the Aiken / North Augusta area. The church is currently in pulpit transition: Greg Williams is listed as senior pastor on ChurchSpring pages but a pastor-search page is also active, and a separate source identifies William L. Watson as interim or successor. Per primary-source report from MOOP Directory editor Adam Johns (who knows Williams personally), Williams was asked to resign and given severance over biblically-sound, orthodoxically-defensible conservative views the congregation's leadership found unwelcome. The church's published statement of faith claims subscription to both BF&M 2000 and the 1646 LBCF — an unusually strong confessional claim — but is silent on women in ministry, marriage, and sexuality. The combination of (a) a conservative pastor being asked to step down despite holding orthodox views, (b) confessional-claim silence on the disputed-third-rail issues of the moment, and (c) confused dual-confession citation suggests a posture more 'institutional-historic' than 'confessionally-orthodox.' YELLOW with documented reasons. Reverify after pulpit settles.
